clue.text: Capital one invested in a new casino

indicators.note: money invested in something goes inside it, so the first piece is placed within the second
a new version of the word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone puts a single unit of money into a newly opened gambling house.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of casino are rearranged as NICOSA and the I slips in before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the seat of government of Cyprus, so it is a national capital city.

indicators.note: altering changes the arrangement, so the letters are shifted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor changing lines for no good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanely means in a silly, empty way, without sense or purpose.

clue.text: Head leaves the platform in resentment

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and leaving means it is removed

blocks.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: A leader walks off the stage in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a person in charge, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread hatred or disgust directed at someone, a strong form of bitterness.

clue.text: Painting technique Pam is to become involved in

indicators.note: things that become involved get entangled, so the letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pam is going to take up a particular method of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pam is to' reads as a plan for Pam; all three words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the application of paint in thick layers so brushstrokes stand out.

blocks.note: pop is an informal word for father
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Father stared in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pop-eyed has eyes bulging with surprise, an idiom for being astonished.

clue.text: Hungry boy - or about to be

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to live is to exist, to be

explanation.surface: A boy who is hungry now, or soon will be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to be' reads as soon-to-be, but splits into a container signal and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is Dickens's workhouse orphan, famously hungry enough to ask for more gruel.

blocks.note: easy means without pain or difficulty
going is a euphemism for dying

explanation.surface: A peaceful, pain-free end to life.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy-going person is relaxed and placid, unworried by things.

clue.text: Presumably, I get a lift during this tour

definitions.text: Presumably, I get a lift during this tour

blocks.clueFragment: Presumably, I get a lift during this tour
blocks.note: surface reading: someone expects to be given a ride while travelling
setter's reading: the self, the I, gets a boost from a self-indulgent venture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' sounds like a ride in a car, but it is a boost to self-esteem; the I is the self.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an activity pursued mainly to flatter one's own vanity and sense of importance.

clue.text: Where strain will cause a parting

definitions.text: Where strain will cause a parting

blocks.clueFragment: Where strain will cause a parting
blocks.note: surface reading: the stage at which tension in a relationship makes a couple separate
setter's reading: a physical rupture, the spot where a stressed material snaps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Parting' suggests lovers separating; read literally it is a material giving way under load.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the limit of stress at which something gives way, literally or emotionally.

clue.text: Transport will be back at eleven

indicators.note: going back means the short word beside it is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A promise that the car will return to collect you at eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired vehicle, one form of transport for passengers.

indicators.note: something wrong is not in its proper order, so the letters must be put right by rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to go away giving a misleading idea of yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as a verb but is the noun, as in shore leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave as a noun means consent or authorisation to do something, as in 'by your leave'.

clue.text: Greek god, part herald, part messenger

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word is taken, here its opening three letters

blocks.note: the first three letters of herald
the first three letters of messenger

explanation.surface: A Greek deity described as partly a herald and partly a messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'part' does the same job for messenger. The surface is also true: Hermes was the herald and messenger of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes is the Olympian deity of travellers and thieves, messenger of Zeus.

clue.text: They returned hurt, watched on 60s' TV

blocks.note: first meaning: people who pay back an injury with revenge
second meaning: the British spy series starring Steed and Mrs Peel

explanation.surface: People who came back injured, seen on television in the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' means repaid, not came back. The Avengers was a British 1960s spy series with John Steed and Emma Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who take revenge repay harm done to them, and the title also names a classic television show.

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at how tuneful Chopin's music is.
explanation.definitionFit: Symphonic describes harmonious orchestral music, close to tuneful in a loose sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: wild, as if controlled by a demon
second meaning: owned, in someone's ownership

explanation.walkthrough: 'Being had' suggests being cheated, but it simply means owned.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessed describes someone frenzied as if by a spirit, and also anything that is owned.

blocks.note: first meaning: quick and agile
second meaning: sharply cold

explanation.surface: Weather turning cold quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a small nimble car is nippy, and so is biting cold weather that nips the skin.

clue.text: Pass out with many a twitch

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many

explanation.surface: Someone faints, with many a jerk of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' reads as fainting, but the two words split into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary muscle contraction, which is what a twitch is.

clue.text: A plain repair I made a mess of

indicators.note: making a mess of something throws it into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone botched a straightforward mending job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like the adjective simple, but it is the noun for flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large area of flat grassland, especially in North America.

definitions.note: a plural noun for a singular one: an aggregate is a whole made up of many parts

indicators.note: assembling means putting pieces together into a new arrangement, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking a car repair shop to put the components together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assemble parts' reads as one instruction, but the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is a mass formed by gathering many separate units or elements together.

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the adjective in the title Revised Version

blocks.note: first meaning: corrected and amended
second meaning: the ... Version, the 1880s English translation

explanation.surface: An amended translation of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means altered after review, and is the first word of the Victorian Bible translation's title.

blocks.note: first meaning: things that grant entry
second meaning: things an inspector clips holes in

explanation.surface: People who confess and then frequently get hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' suggests confessing, and 'punched' suggests violence; both apply to passes clipped by an inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Passes for travel or events let the holder enter, and conductors clip holes in them.

clue.text: Give the signal to pass a bottle of wine

blocks.note: to flag is to signal, as with a waved flag
on, as in waving someone on to go past

explanation.surface: Someone signals for the wine to be handed round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: To flag someone on is to wave them through.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel with a handle and spout for serving wine or cider.

indicators.note: letters that exchange places swap around into a new order
one piece sits in the other, enclosed by it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Subsequent exchanges in a court of law over a legal fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb meaning to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo was the 1815 battle where Wellington defeated Napoleon.

clue.text: 5 to 4 on the winner that's lively

blocks.note: V is five in Roman numerals
IV is four in Roman numerals
an ace in tennis is a winning serve

explanation.surface: Betting odds of five to four laid on the horse that is the most spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 to 4 on' reads as betting odds, but the numbers are Roman numerals joined in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivace is a musical direction meaning play briskly and in a spirited manner.

blocks.note: surface reading: a man who loves going to social gatherings
setter's reading: political parties canvass a person at election time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' suggests celebrations, but it means political parties seeking support.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a member of the electorate whose ballot candidates try to win at elections.

blocks.note: surface reading: people who won the admiration of veteran seamen
setter's reading: to impress is also to force men into naval service, as these press parties did

explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' suggests admiration, but its old sense is forcible enlistment in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: These were bands of men who seized civilians and compelled them to serve aboard warships.

clue.text: English flower seen on the golf course

blocks.note: first meaning: a river in north-east England; a flower is something that flows
second meaning: the pegs or starting areas golfers drive from

explanation.surface: A bloom from England growing on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, something that flows. The Tees runs through Teesside to the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a northern English river and the plural of the peg a golf ball rests on.

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Something crooked at its forward end.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who is ahead of the field is in first position, heading the race.

blocks.note: first meaning: to direct remarks at someone
second meaning: where a person lives, as written on a letter

explanation.surface: Talking to one's house.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for formally speaking to an audience and a noun for the place of residence.
